acceptanceCriteria: Each docs corpus local-input refusal names the flag and the violated rule (absolute, parent traversal, non-canonical), code unchanged, covered by focused tests.
docs corpus help and the owning spec state that local inputs are root-relative, verified by a help test.
body:
Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#796.

Observed: `docs corpus` commands that read local inputs through the bounded reader (e.g. discover-playwright --migration/--playwright-list) refuse an absolute path with only `{"code":"corpus-refused","error":"invalid local input path"}`. Inputs must be canonical paths relative to --root (no leading /, no .., cleaned), but neither the error nor the help says so; an automated caller retried the same refused command across sessions.

Expected: the refusal names the offending flag and the rule (e.g. `--migration: input paths must be relative to --root (got an absolute path)`), keeping the stable code; `docs corpus` help states that --migration, --playwright-list, --receipt and similar inputs are root-relative and must sit under --root.

completion.reason: Delivered in beamfall/corvint#801 (https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/pull/801; landed by batch PR #801); on main at 8f032d969f26dc0d3bd10ec0248566070161272d (https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/pull/801). Tests named in the PR: DCP-V1-054 corpus input-path refusal tests. Doc gates, repin check, independent review and dogfood bind/check/seal reported PASS in the PR. make gate NOT_RUN (owner scoped-work preference). Evidence: sha256 of the build-log/decision record(s) at the merge commit.

title: docs corpus: 'invalid local input path' does not name the flag or the root-relative rule (GH #796)
